prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: at which hours of the day, in Amsterdam time, do web orders come in? Use the orders table and keep the orders with channel 'web'. order_ts holds the time of the order in UTC: turn it into Amsterdam time first, then take the hour. Return two columns, in this order: order_hour, the Amsterdam hour from 0 to 23, and orders, the number of web orders. Return one row for each hour. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, look at order_hour: it is the hour on a UTC clock, not on an Amsterdam clock.
Amsterdam is 1 or 2 hours ahead of UTC, depending on the season. Turn order_ts into Amsterdam time with the two timezone calls before you take the hour, in SELECT and in GROUP BY.
starter_sql:
SELECT hour(order_ts) AS order_hour, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
GROUP BY hour(order_ts)
why_this_works: Converting order_ts to Amsterdam time before taking the hour puts every order at the hour an Amsterdam clock showed, in winter and in summer time.
